items.fact: The campaign is split into five chapters, and PC Gamer's mission list counts 91 story missions (other outlets count 93, so totals differ by source).
Chapters unlock in order once you finish every mission in the previous chapter, and finished missions can't be replayed.

Chapter 1 is centered on the Leonida Keys, chapter 2 on Port Gellhorn, chapters 3 and 4 on Vice City, and the 7-mission chapter 5 on Vice City and wider Leonida. A full playthrough of the main missions can run 65–70 hours.
You follow two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a criminal duo caught in a conspiracy across Leonida.
The game is set in Leonida, Rockstar's fictional Florida, and Vice City is its biggest city.
Leonida is divided into five counties, and collectible cards are scattered across all of them.
There are 18 collectible card sets (most with 24 cards, others 12 to 36), and you can track them under Progress Collections in the touchpad menu.
There are 33 Underwater Discovery sites, many containing Kenton's Treasures, which you dig up with a metal detector and sell to Kenton.
WAiNK collectibles come as 35 Curiosities, 31 Landmarks and 23 Sculptures.
There are 27 magazines, books and comics to find, counted separately from book swaps.
100% completion needs 8 vaults hit, 15 meditation spots, 100 cocaine flamingos destroyed, 5 Kenton sets and 70 of the 80 challenges, with more than 160 animals in the world.
There are 40 unique race locations, and winning a race pays more than the entry and vehicle rental fees cost.
From Chapter 2, Moses buys stolen cars without trackers for roughly $1,000–$5,000 each, and from mid-Chapter 3 Randy pays $30,000 or more for supercars on his 18-car wish list.
Rival gang hideouts are a strong earner. Forbes says that once they respawn they can pay about $10,000–$30,000 per run, and the big vault always returns.
Win Demolition Derby events at Ambrosia Raceway for roughly $3,800–$6,300 per win, since you finish first by default when the other cars are wrecked.
Chapter 1 fences Brian and Donnie pay only very low or low rates. Selling narcotics to Donnie after the mission Clean Up After Donnie is an effective early money-maker.
Robbing banks and loan stores is best left until Chapter 3, because dye packs explode unless you have a dye pack jammer.
Check the map for back doors, since the snap gun lets you enter without triggering alarms. Medium- or high-security robberies are much easier as a pair.
Public buses and trains give cheaper fast travel than RydeMe, but they run on schedules so you have to wait for them.
Stolen cars carry trackers: Moses won't take cars with trackers, and Pay 'n' Spray won't take cars with a high-end tracker.
Rockstar shipped two pre-launch updates, on Nov 13 and Nov 16 (01.002.001), and published no patch notes for either.
A glitch lets players get stuck in first-person view even though the game launched without a first-person mode, and the only way out is to reload the save.
A money exploit at Brian's Lockup in Key Lento, which uses stash bags and a save/reload loop, earned about $8,000 every 5 minutes. Game Rant presents it as something to use before it's patched.
